name: Morocco
system_note: The king holds most real power; an elected government handles day-to-day policy.
snapshot: A September 2026 election produced Morocco's first woman head of government, while real power stays with the king and a Gen Z protest movement demands better schools and hospitals.
culture: Morocco blends Arab, Amazigh and Andalusian influences, and Tamazight became an official language in 2011. The medinas of Fez and Marrakech, Gnawa trance music with roots in West Africa, and a cuisine of tagines and couscous draw millions of visitors. The national football team's run to the 2022 World Cup semi-final was a moment of pride across the Arab world and Africa.
society: The king controls defence, foreign policy and religion, and is officially Commander of the Faithful. Morocco is building high-speed rail and stadiums for the 2030 World Cup it will co-host with Spain and Portugal. Youth unemployment is high, and the 2025 Gen Z 212 protests contrasted stadium spending with crumbling hospitals. Its claim to Western Sahara has won growing international backing.
situation: In September 2025, eight pregnant women died at a public hospital in Agadir. The deaths set off Morocco's largest protests in years, led by a leaderless online movement calling itself GenZ 212, whose chant, "We want hospitals, not just stadiums," hit at a government spending billions on the 2030 World Cup. The protesters appealed directly to King Mohammed VI and demanded that Prime Minister Aziz Akhannouch, a billionaire businessman, resign (KAS). A year later, Moroccans got their answer at the ballot box, in a way.

In the 23 September election, Akhannouch's RNI fell to 66 seats. Its coalition partner, the Party of Authenticity and Modernity (PAM), came first with 97, boosted by recruiting Fouzi Lekjaa, the head of the football federation, weeks before the vote (Reuters via TimesLive). Turnout was just 38 percent, the lowest since 2007, a sign that many young people still do not see elections as the place where change happens (Kuwait Times). On 29 September, the king appointed PAM's Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, a lawyer and former Marrakech mayor, as Morocco's first woman head of government. Her government will oversee the last stretch of a $20 billion World Cup build-out, the same spending the protesters questioned.
power: A constitutional monarchy where the king holds most real power, controlling defence, foreign affairs, religion and security. He must appoint the head of government from the party that wins most seats in the 395-seat House of Representatives, and the government handles domestic policy.
holders: King Mohammed VI, since 1999; Head of Government Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, whose coalition took office on 16 October 2026.

update.html: On 16 October the four-party coalition government of Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri took office. The king named her head of government on 29 September, making her the first woman to hold the post.
